34112.en: On page 18 of **Jean-Pierre Ehrmann,** `Congruent Inscribed Rectangles <http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2002volume2/FG200203.pdf>`__, a circle is described. For any μ > 0, the circle, which passes through points X_100, X_106 and a certain point P(μ), is here named the **μ-Ehrmann circle**. Its center is given by
no: a^2*(b - c)*(b*c*(a + b + c)*(a^3 - a^2*b - a*b^2 + b^3 - a^2*c + 5*a*b*c - 2*b^2*c - a*c^2 - 2*b*c^2 + c^3) - ((a - b)*(a - c)*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)*S)/μ) : : This center lies on the line {3,2827} and is given by the combos (r/μ - s) X[3] + s X[4491] = ((a + b + c)^2 - 2 S/μ) X[3] - (a + b + c)^2 X[4491]. X_34112 is obtained by putting μ = 1. (Peter Moses, July 15, 2019)
